topics.title: Chapter 1: Real Numbers
topics.description: Euclid's Division Lemma, HCF, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, and Decimal Expansions.

cards.heading: Euclid's Division Lemma
cards.conceptText: For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

steps: Here dividend a = 17, divisor b = 5, quotient q = 3, remainder r = 2.

cards.keyTakeaway: The remainder r is always non-negative and strictly smaller than the divisor b.

cards.heading: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
cards.conceptText: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorization is unique apart from the order in which prime factors occur.
cards.keyTakeaway: Prime factorization gives the unique foundational building blocks of any number.

topics.title: Chapter 2: Polynomials
topics.description: Geometrical meaning of zeroes, relationship between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic polynomials.

cards.heading: Zeroes of a Polynomial
cards.conceptText: A real number k is a zero of polynomial p(x) if p(k) = 0. Graphically, zeroes are the x-coordinates of points where y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
cards.keyTakeaway: A polynomial of degree n can have at most n zeroes.

questions.text: In Euclid's Division Lemma a = bq + r, which condition must remainder 'r' satisfy?
hintLadder: Remainder cannot be negative, so it must be at least 0.
If remainder equals divisor b, you can divide once more! So r cannot equal b.
Therefore, 0 ≤ r < b. Correct option is B.
questions.explanation: According to Euclid's Division Lemma, 0 ≤ r < b. Remainder cannot equal or exceed divisor b.

questions.text: What is the HCF of 45 and 15 using Euclid's algorithm?
hintLadder: Divide 45 by 15.
Since the remainder is 0, the divisor 15 is the HCF.
questions.explanation: Since 45 = 15 × 3 + 0, the remainder is 0 and HCF is 15.

questions.text: What is the prime factorization of 140?
hintLadder: Prime factors must only contain prime numbers (no 70, 35, 14, 4).
All factors (2, 5, 7) are prime. Option B is correct.

questions.text: A rational number p/q has a terminating decimal expansion if the prime factorization of denominator q is of the form:
hintLadder: Decimal system is base 10.
Factors of 10 are 2 and 5.
So denominator must only have factors of 2 and 5 (2^n × 5^m).
questions.explanation: A decimal terminates if and only if the denominator's prime factors are only 2 and 5 (q = 2^n × 5^m).

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is an irrational number?
hintLadder: √4 = 2 and √9 = 3 (both are integers, so rational).
0.25 = 1/4 (rational).
5 is not a perfect square, so √5 cannot be written as p/q.
questions.explanation: √5 is irrational because 5 is a prime number and not a perfect square.

questions.text: What is the zero of the linear polynomial p(x) = 2x + 6?
hintLadder: To find the zero, set p(x) = 0.

questions.text: For a quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c with zeroes α and β, the sum of zeroes (α + β) equals:
hintLadder: Sum of zeroes has a minus sign with the coefficient of x.
α + β = -(coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x²).
Therefore, α + β = -b/a.
questions.explanation: Sum of zeroes α + β = -b/a. Product of zeroes αβ = c/a.

mistakeRemedies.included_equal_to_b: The remainder can never equal the divisor b; it must always be strictly less than b (r < b).
mistakeRemedies.excluded_zero: The remainder can be 0 when a number is perfectly divisible (0 ≤ r).
mistakeRemedies.remainder_larger_than_divisor: The remainder cannot be larger than the divisor.
mistakeRemedies.included_composite_70: Prime factorization cannot include composite numbers like 70.
mistakeRemedies.included_prime_3: Factors of 3 create non-terminating recurring decimals.
mistakeRemedies.sign_error_positive_3: Remember to change the sign when moving +6 across the equals sign to get -6.
mistakeRemedies.forgot_minus_sign: Sum of zeroes has a negative sign: -b/a.
mistakeRemedies.product_of_zeroes_c_over_a: c/a is the product of zeroes (αβ), not the sum.

commonDoubts.q: How to check if a fraction has a terminating decimal?
commonDoubts.a: First reduce the fraction to lowest terms. Then factorize the denominator q. If q has only 2s and 5s (2^n × 5^m), it terminates. If any other prime factor like 3, 7, 11 appears, it is non-terminating.

commonDoubts.q: What is the difference between HCF and LCM?
commonDoubts.a: HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the product of the smallest powers of each common prime factor. LCM (Least Common Multiple) is the product of the greatest powers of all prime factors. Also: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

commonDoubts.q: What are zeroes of a polynomial?
commonDoubts.a: The zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the values of x for which p(x) becomes 0. On a graph, they are the exact points where the curve crosses the horizontal x-axis.
